title: Gemological Practice Standard: Arriving at and Recording Value, Belrose Appraisal and Gemological Services
content:
# Gemological Practice Standard: Arriving at and Recording Value

**Approach.** The value under Belrose Appraisal and Gemological Services is arrived at on the approach the service uses: what it would cost to replace the piece new (replacement cost new), what comparable pieces have sold for (comparable sales), what it would fetch on a forced sale (liquidation), or the laboratory's own grading (laboratory grading). Which approach a service uses is fixed per service.

**Stage of recording.** A value is recorded only while the engagement stands in examination, report drafted or issued, and each piece is valued once on an engagement. The stage is read from the engagement record under its appraisal reference, and the record is what governs.

**Testing and assay.** The stones are tested rather than accepted as described at the services that include gemological testing, and the metal is assayed rather than taken from the hallmark at the services that include an assay. Whether the report plots the inclusions of the principal stone, whether it carries photographs, and whether it is prepared to the Uniform Standards of Professional Appraisal Practice or to a standard a court will receive are likewise fixed per service.

**Outside laboratory.** Where the service sends the stone to an outside laboratory, the value rests on that laboratory's grading and the report names which laboratory it was.

**The customer's belief.** The customer's own belief about what the piece is worth is recorded as context and never stands in for the value the appraiser arrives at.

## Stage at which a value is recorded

| Engagement stands at | Value recorded |
|---|---|
| Requested | No |
| Item received | No |
| In examination | Yes |
| Report drafted | Yes |
| Issued | Yes |
| Delivered | No |
| Expired | No |
| Cancelled | No |

## Cases

- An engagement stands in examination and no value has yet been recorded for the piece: a value is recorded.
- An engagement stands at report drafted and a value is already recorded for the piece: a second value for that piece on that engagement is not recorded, because each piece is valued once on an engagement.
- An engagement stands at item received: the value is not recorded until the engagement stands in examination.
- A customer states what they believe the piece is worth and asks that the figure be taken as the value: the belief is recorded as context, and the value the appraiser arrives at on the service's approach is the value the report states.
- A stone was sent to an outside laboratory under a service that sends stones out: the value rests on that laboratory's grading, and the report names the laboratory.
